title: Man. Post. Cap. III: non urgeor — culpa common by propagation; vitium; not properly poena
pass_a_gloss: By these absurdities I am not hard pressed, who want the guilt to be as common to all as the penalty: common, I say, in the thing itself, not by imputation but by propagation, and to be imputed to us because it is within us. But that guilt is the original vice inhering in each of us, which itself I do not want to be a penalty properly speaking, for those reasons which I will presently open in the following chapter.
pass_b_english: These absurdities do not press me. I hold that the guilt is as common to all as the penalty—common in the thing itself, not by imputation but by propagation—and that it is imputed to us because it is within us. That guilt is the original vice inhering in each of us. I refuse to call that vice a penalty in the proper sense, for reasons I will open in the next chapter.
source_text: His ego absurdis non urgeor, qui culpam volo esse tam communem omnibus, quam poenam: communem inquam reapse, non imputatione sed propagatione, ac nobis imputari, quia intra nos est. Culpa autem illa est vitium originale nobis singulis inhaerens, quam ipsam nolo proprie loquendo poenam esse ob eas causas, quas mox aperiam cap. sequente.
